attacks.claim: The design needs 160 req/min of real-time chain data, but the chosen Starter tier allows 5 req/min with 15-min delayed quotes. Growth ($199 + $60 VPS = $259) breaks the $250 cap and is still under 160 req/min. Only Pro ($499 + $60 = $559) satisfies the rate limit, which violates the agreed constraint. The '$139 comfortably inside the cap' budget is for a tier that cannot run the design.
attacks.evidence: "Starter | $79 | 5 req/min | 15-min delayed" vs "40 underlyings => 160 requests/min during RTH" and "We stay on Starter."

attacks.claim: Starter quotes are 15 minutes delayed, so delta, extrinsic and gap triggers and mid-limit pricing would be evaluated on stale data. The premise of capturing intraday mean-reversion windows cannot work, and live orders could be priced off stale quotes.
attacks.evidence: "Starter ... 15-min delayed" vs "fetch a real-time option chain snapshot"

attacks.claim: Migration 0042 drops roll_history in prod in place, and backfills only 90 days, so older roll history is permanently lost. No backup, restore check or down-migration is specified. The roll_eod.py fallback is kept 'through week 4', but if it reads roll_history it breaks the moment the column is dropped.
attacks.evidence: "In the same transaction, ALTER TABLE positions DROP COLUMN roll_history." ... "roll_eod.py stays deployed behind ROLLER_V2=false as the fallback path"

attacks.claim: The plan discards roll history older than 90 days for a family-office account. That history may be needed for tax-lot, cost-basis, audit or recordkeeping purposes, and the plan does not check this. Deciding it is 'not needed by roll_engine' is not the right test.
attacks.evidence: "older entries are not needed by roll_engine"

attacks.claim: The +3.8% net APR headline has no backtest or measurement. It rests on anecdotal desk notes and an unsourced claim about other funds, yet it is the success criterion. Paper mode logs intents, not fills, so it cannot validate the economics, and 30 live days is too noisy to detect the effect.
attacks.evidence: "Expected impact: +3.8% net APR" ... "Desk notes ... 'would have been better'" ... "RollIntent written, no orders"

attacks.claim: Roll target rules don't bound cost: the same-strike roll has no minimum credit or max debit, so a debit roll can be sent. When the combo is cancelled after 3 reprices, nothing says how an ITM short call at delta >= 0.70 is handled, and the 1-roll-per-contract-per-day cap may block retries.
attacks.evidence: "same strike +1 expiry, or next strike up if the credit is >= $0.05" ... "re-priced every 20 s up to 3 times, then cancelled"

attacks.claim: The outage handling only stops new intents. It doesn't cover working combo orders, market-data failure or staleness, or alerting and on-call response. No metrics or alerts are planned for a system that places live orders.
attacks.evidence: "roll_engine stops emitting intents when the last successful broker heartbeat is > 60 s old."

attacks.claim: An env-var kill switch 'read on every loop' does not change in a running process, since environment variables are fixed at start, so it likely needs a restart. The emergency stop is under-specified.
attacks.evidence: "ROLLER_KILL env switch read on every loop"

attacks.claim: The plan refers to 'positions table changes in §5' but §5 defines none. Two roll paths are kept live with no removal plan.
There is no description of broker credential handling or validation of vendor data before it triggers live orders.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: credential storage and input validation

attacks.claim: Execution-critical data comes from a single vendor with no fallback feed.
